title: Basis Questions on Repeat Status Awards and the Summit Gold Price (Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements)
content:
**What sets the Gold repeat-award percentage on a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement?**
The status awards already redeemed on the agreement in the Gold award window — the 12 calendar months up to and including the redemption date — set it:

| Status awards already redeemed on the agreement in the window | Gold repeat-award percentage |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 130 percent |
| exactly 1 | 115 percent |
| none | 100 percent (the full price) |

**Which redemptions count?**
Every status-award redemption entry on the agreement's points activity dated inside the window — Summit Silver and Summit Gold alike, for any roster traveler. Award tickets and upgrades are not status awards and do not count.

**How does the percentage act on the price?**
The Gold repeat-award percentage multiplies the standard Gold award price, the tier's Summit Gold status-award points. Where the price carries several such percentages, they are all applied together to the standard price, each divided by one hundred, and the product is rounded to the nearest whole point once.

**What does an agreement with one earlier status award pay, with no other percentage on the price? (hypothetical)**
On a standard price of 3800 points, 3800 multiplied by 115 and divided by one hundred: 4370 points.

**Does a status award redeemed more than 12 months before the redemption date count?**
No; only redemptions inside the 12-month window count.
